title: Emu Bay Shale Lagerstätte, Kangaroo Island
summary: The Emu Bay Shale on the northern coast of Kangaroo Island, South Australia, preserves soft-bodied animals from about 514–509 million years ago, in Cambrian Series 2, Stage 4. At Big Gully it yields giant Anomalocaris-like predators, trilobites and arthropods, and is described as Australia's only Cambrian Konservat-Lagerstätte of this kind.

uncertainty.note: Age given as approximately 514-509 Ma on the Heritage Council document; no numerical age on the Palaeontology paper page.

when.display: about 514–509 million years ago (Cambrian Series 2, Stage 4)

where.historical_name: Emu Bay Shale, a marine basin on the margin of East Gondwana (no polities exist at this date)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point -35.58, 137.50 reconstructed to 514 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 12.59 N, 159.67 W (about 16 degrees of latitude and 70 degrees of longitude away). MULLER2019 covers only 0-250 Ma and returned an error for 514 Ma. The wide model spread reflects differing absolute reference frames.

importance.justification: Australia's only Burgess Shale-type fossil deposit, showing early Cambrian predators and arthropods in East Gondwana.

reviewer_note: The record id uses -514 Ma; the Heritage Council document gives the span 514-509 Ma, the only numerical age on an opened page. The Journal of the Geological Society review (514 +/- 1 Ma) could not be opened. Coordinates are the Wikidata point for the formation (on the north coast near Emu Bay); Big Gully is the fossil locality, within a few km. Model spread for the paleo-position is large; Merdith 2021 is the stored value.
